core_obligations: Use quasi-compactness to choose finitely many elements whose principal opens cover the closed subset defined by the ideal, with the localisations generated by quasi-regular sequences (proof lines 8144-8148).
Write the local generators as fractions with denominators powers of the localising elements and lift them to elements of the ideal (proof lines 8148-8152).

Produce an element x of the ideal with 1 + x in the ideal generated by the localising elements, and conclude that the lifted generators together with x generate the ideal on every piece of the cover (proof lines 8152-8157).
proof_roadmap: Choose the finite cover and the local quasi-regular sequences (proof lines 8144-8148).
Lift the local generators to the ideal (proof lines 8148-8152).
Add the element x and conclude with the cover lemma (proof lines 8152-8157).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a quasi-regular ideal is finitely generated, and the proof is a 14-line argument that reduces the question to a finite cover of the spectrum. It uses the quasi-compactness of the closed subset defined by the ideal to choose finitely many localising elements over which the localised ideal is generated by a quasi-regular sequence, lifts the local generators back to elements of the ideal, and then adds one further element obtained from a Bezout style relation to obtain a generating set on every piece of the cover. The construction of the cover and the lifting of the generators are the two steps, and both are displayed.
